title: Shop promise cost: a hard break pays the promise cost of the step limit
eyebrow: reward layer · shop levels · plan check · 2026-11-20
subtitle: Every shop run that learned had an open promise that cost something as the step limit ran out: the promise cost or the end judgment (12 of 12 seeds served; with both off, 0 of 12). With the promise cost on and a well the agent can reach, the step into the well ended the episode without the promise cost still to come, so letting the food fall paid more than serving. Commit `a727b2b` charges the step into the well the promise cost of the whole step limit (-10.1 becomes -70 on the shop). The round 7 level still learns as before (12.21 / 12.07 / 12.21 served). Today's shop-serve still learns 0 of 3: an open question for the user, not a result. The same commit replaces the no-goal plan check: 35 of the 38 no-goal bundles the old rule failed by construction now pass, and the new rule finds a real defect in forcing/lanes-rules.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: A shop task is a set of promises: when a client comes in, the agent owes an order, food and the serve. The Reward Machine pays the agent as it keeps each promise. Two optional switches price a promise left open. The **promise cost** charges -0.1 for every step a hard promise is open. The **end judgment** charges each hard promise still open when the episode stops. The **well** is the machine's dead state: a hard rule broken for good pays -10 there and the episode ends. On today's shop levels the hard rule an agent can break for good is the fall rule: "if the food falls, pick it up on your very next move". The step limit is 600.

items: **Why the earlier runs learned.** Learning needs an open promise to cost something as the step limit runs out. With both switches off, a whole shift of serving pays 0 and taking one order then stopping pays -2 (round 6, seed 1): the 2-point gap does not grow with the clients served, and no seed learned to serve.

**The defect.** With the promise cost on, the step into the well paid -10 and one step of promise cost, -10.1, then the episode ended. The promise cost of every step that never came went unpaid, so dropping the food paid more than serving on all four shop levels: -16.4 against -35.5 plain on shop-serve, seed 1.

**The fix.** The step into the well now pays the promise cost of the whole step limit: -10 - 0.1 × 600 = -70 on the shop. After it the solve is the best plan on all eight level variants. With the promise cost off every machine is byte-identical: the two committed sweeps and the four levels.
**No regression.** The round 7 level trains to 12.21 / 12.07 / 12.21 served with the fix, identical to round 7 B8b. Its level has no slip, so its machine has no well and its text did not change.

**Open.** Today's shop-serve, promise cost on and the fix in, serves 0 on 3 of 3 seeds. Random play never prepares food in 1,000 episodes, and the trained agents never pick the food up. The options wait for the user (Part 4).

**The no-goal plan check.** With the end judgment off, the old rule failed 38 of 62 no-goal bundles by construction. The new rule passes 35 of them, leaves the 275 goal bundles unchanged, catches a shop-serve built without its fall rule on 3 of 3 seeds and finds a real defect in the committed forcing/lanes-rules.

sections.title: 1. Why the earlier shop runs learned
sections.intro: Every run trains PPO on the shop with the machine's reward only, gamma 0.995, learning rate 0.001, one-hot machine state, 3 seeds, judged on 100 test episodes. Served is the mean number of clients served per test episode (`check/runs_table.py`, `evidence/runs.out`). Plan pay is the machine's reward for a scripted plan of the card on its first event seed, plain / discounted at 0.995 (`check/plan_pay.py rounds`, `evidence/part1-rounds.json`, seeds 2 and 3 there too). Rounds 6 and 7 trained 2M steps with a -5 time-limit charge; the probe 5M steps without one. Plan pay leaves that charge out: it is the same on every plan that runs to the step limit.

items: **The PPO settings are not the cause.** r6-A, B and C train one machine with PPO clip 0.2 or 0.1 and value clipping on or off: all serve 0. r6-D and r6-E keep the clauses and change one reward switch: they serve 11 to 18 clients.

**Both off, serving pays almost nothing more.** A client's arrival pays -3, one point for each promise it opens, and each kept promise pays its point back. So a whole shift of serving nets 0, taking the first order and stopping -2, idling -3. The gap is 2 points plain, about 1.3 discounted, whatever the number of clients served. The probe's trained agents took the first order and stopped (plan log, 2026-11-20 19:24).

**Promise cost on, every open step costs.** Idling leaves a promise open for about 600 steps, -61.6; serving closes each one quickly, -20.8. The gap, about 40 points plain and 11.7 discounted, grows with each client served.

**End judgment on, the end charges what is open.** Each hard promise open when the episode stops pays -10: idle -33, serving 0. Discounted at step 600 (0.995^600 is about 0.05) the gap shrinks to 3.6, and it still trained.

**None of these machines has a well.** The round 6 and 7 levels have no slip (`slip_chance` 0), so their cards carry no fall rule and their machines no rejecting state (`evidence/machines.out`: 0 edges into the well). The defect of Part 2 could not show there.

sections.title: 2. The defect and the fix
sections.intro: Today's shop levels add the slip and the fall rule, hard `ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food)`: a fall the agent does not save on its very next move breaks the rule for good, and the machine enters the well, which ends the episode. Plan pay as in Part 1, on the four shop levels built from their card answers with the promise cost on and off, before (the code of `78c666c`, a727b2b's parent) and after (`a727b2b`): `check/plan_pay.py levels`, `evidence/part2-before.json`, `evidence/part2-after.json`, `evidence/pay-table.out`.

blocks.title: The defect, before a727b2b
blocks.text: With the promise cost on, the step into the well paid the well charge and one step of promise cost, -10 - 0.1 = -10.1, and the episode ended. The promise cost of the steps that never came was not charged. So the cheapest shift was to carry the food, let it fall and leave it: -16.4 plain on shop-serve, seed 1, where serving all shift paid -35.5. The probe's gate stopped this machine before training on all four levels (plan log, 2026-11-20 16:16).

blocks.title: The fix, commit a727b2b
blocks.text: The step into the well, from a state with a hard promise open, now pays the promise cost of the level's whole step limit: -10 - 0.1 × 600 = -70 on the shop (`_price_edges` in `app/src/compiler/reward_layer.py`). The fix touches only edges into the well, and only with the promise cost on. A promise-cost build now refuses to run without the level's step limit, and train-rl refuses a promise-cost bundle whose recorded step limit is not the level's.

**The bound.** A break at step t pays γ^t (W + cL), with W = -10 the well charge, c = -0.1 the promise cost and L = 600 the step limit. Since W and c are at most 0, that is at most the sum of γ^k c over k = t to L - 1, the cost of keeping the promise open to the end: a hard break never pays more than a promise kept open. It is a bound, not the exact cost: a late break is charged all L steps, not the L - t left. Whether that reading of "the promise cost still to come" is right is the user's question Q6.

sections.intro: Before training, the gate runs each card's solving, wrong and idle plans through the bundle's machine (`check_card_plans` in `app/src/benchmark/plan_check.py`). A no-goal task has no final state, so no run ever finishes. The old rule failed a wrong run that "ends with nothing owed and out of the well". With the end judgment off nothing is owed at the end, so a no-goal bundle failed whenever a wrong plan stayed out of the well. The new rule adds an idle plan. Every wrong run, and an idle run that breaks a rule of the card, must pay less than the solve on the same layout, plain and discounted, and a run that breaks a hard rule for good must end in the well. An idle run that keeps every rule is held to the solve's rules. Every committed bundle checked before and after (`check/plan_check_all.py`, `check/compare_checks.py`, `evidence/plan-check/`).

**Limits:** the page quotes seed 1 of the card's event seeds; seeds 2 and 3 are in the records.
